**Justification:**

This allocation is considered fair for several reasons:

**1. Pareto Efficiency:**

The allocation is Pareto efficient, meaning that it is not possible to improve the allocation for any one person without making someone else worse off.

**2. Envy-Freeness:**

Neither Person 2 nor Person 3 would prefer the allocation received by the other person. This is because Person 2 values Good A and Good D more than any other combination of two goods, and Person 3 values Good B and Good C more than any other combination of two goods.

**3. Equity:**

The allocation considers the individual values of the goods. Person 2 places a higher value on Good A and Good D, so they receive those goods. Person 3 places a higher value on Good B and Good C, so they receive those goods. You receive Good A and Good B, which have the highest combined value for you.

**4. Acceptability:**

The allocation is likely to be acceptable to all participants because it considers their individual values and does not allocate any goods that they value highly to someone else.

**Additional Note:**

It is important to note that this allocation is not the only fair allocation possible. However, it is an allocation that meets the criteria of Pareto efficiency, envy-freeness, equity, and acceptability.
